<reason>Both sides argued tightly and stayed on the motion as written, with CON correctly narrowing the clash to filling and drought-year operation rather than the dam's existence. The decisive exchange was PRO's pressure question: absent a signature, who decides? CON answered "No" twice — Egypt's refusal is not a perpetual halt, yet Ethiopia may not proceed while the objection is live — without ever naming the third mechanism or arbiter that resolves the gap. PRO's closing crystallized that as a veto with no off-switch, and also landed the symmetry point CON only half-absorbed: CON demanded that Ethiopia be bound by unsigned constraints while conceding that unsigned Egyptian demands bind nobody. CON's best work (staged filling occurred in cooperating seasons and does not simulate successive dry years; evaporation savings are a decades ledger, not water that fails to arrive this season; generation incentive is a motive to hold when the lake is low) genuinely damaged PRO's empirical comfort and produced the most memorable weighing line of the debate ("delayed light can wait a season; missing Nile flow cannot"). But PRO answered its own pressure question honestly by biting the bullet, kept the non-consumptive/throughput mechanism alive, and left CON's operative rule underspecified at exactly the scenario the motion describes. Minor discipline cost to PRO for asserting "no answer came" to a question CON had not yet had a turn to answer.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's exploitation of CON's double "No" in Rebuttal 2: by denying both that refusal alone halts filling and that Ethiopia may proceed while the objection is live, CON left no exit condition, allowing PRO to show that a renewable objection functions as a permanent veto in a basin with no referee.</best_rebuttal>
